nodes.author: IEnakhena
nodes.text: @sunrisedailynow The Northern states of Zamfara & Sokoto has a weak security system, and the federal and state governments have a weak institutional capacity for forest management. These states has many ungoverned spaces that bandits use for criminal activities and capacity building, while Successive political leaders in Nigeria have offered poor quality governance

nodes.author: IEnakhena
nodes.text: @sunrisedailynow Environmental degradation and scarcity of water and arable land have led to communities competing for resources. The state's agricultural and economic potential has been challenged by population growth and environmental degradation. This has led to a protracted conflict between farmers and herders that has turned to banditry.

nodes.author: IEnakhena
nodes.text: @sunrisedailynow Armed banditry has been linked to several causes among which are, displacement due to civil wars in Nigeria's neighboring countries, lack of basic amenities in the border communities, growing unemployment among youths, and moral decadence both among the youths and other members of the border communities

nodes.author: IEnakhena
nodes.text: @sunrisedailynow Banditry is profit-driven. In Zamfara, it had its roots in the growing demand for meat in Nigeria's cities, which made cattle rustling extremely lucrative. The thefts were originally from within the pastoralist Fulani community, targeting remote forest-based Fulani camps.
